describes: The constants the workflow's prompts and tools read that belong to no one tool: the spelling of the tracker label that marks a product change's epic and every one of its tasks, the three label vocabularies a run leaves in the tracker so that `bd count` can show what recurs across runs, the sizes of the review that `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs on each task of a product change, the markers and thresholds of the batched prompt review (`CLAUDE.md` § Prompt reviews), and what the pull-request reviewer (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`, deciding through `scripts/pr-review.mjs`) reads to decide a merge.
whyThisFileExists: A constant spelled in a register entry, six skills and an agent is eight copies, and the stale one is the one a reader finds. CLAUDE.md § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth puts every constant a tool or a prompt reads in a policy file under a key, with its reason beside it. `docs/decisions.md` § D-02 held the label's spelling only until this file existed; § D-03 moved it here.
gatedBy: npm run openspec:check (this file carries `specChangeLabel` and its `Means` sibling; every skill and agent that spells the label cites the key, and every one that cites the key spells its current value). No gate yet holds `assetLabels`, `foundAtLabels` or `rerouteLabels`: the prompts cite the keys and spell none of their values, and asdlc-openspec-dzi asks `beads:check` to refuse a found issue without them. npm run workflows:selftest holds the four `buildReview*` keys: it runs the workflow against stubbed agents with this file's values, runs a clean control for every `buildReviewLenses` key, and refuses a missing key, a kind that is not an `assetLabels` key and a lens the workflow does not have. No gate holds the four `promptReview*` keys: a run and the reviewer read them from this file, and nothing else spells their values. npm run pr-review:check holds the `prReview*` keys: it refuses a missing key or `Means` sibling, a value of the wrong shape, and a `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` or `.github/workflows/verify.yml` that spells a label, a status context or a check other than this file does; npm run pr-review:selftest runs the reviewer's decisions over fixtures built from these values.
whatItDoesNOTDo: It does not hold a rule about how a run proceeds, which lives in CLAUDE.md or in the skill that runs it: when a label is applied is CLAUDE.md § The task store and § Product work runs as OpenSpec-format changes, and who reads the counts is `.claude/skills/change-finalize/SKILL.md` § 9. Report; how a run writes its analysis and when a review of the analyses starts is CLAUDE.md § Prompt reviews. It computes nothing: `bd count` does the counting. It holds no prompt text: the review's lens prompts and the kinds of finding they report are the workflow's own, and what a finding blocks is `.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 5. What the build turns up. The pull-request reviewer's rubrics are the prose of `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md`, and how its verdict becomes a merge is `scripts/pr-review.mjs`; this file holds only the values both read.
provenance: Written 2026-09-23 under D-03 (asdlc-openspec-4gp), which moved the label's spelling here out of D-02. Each later key carries its date and its evidence in its `Means` sibling; the `prReview*` keys came with D-07 (asdlc-openspec-mi6), and the `promptReview*` keys with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
specChangeLabelMeans: The tracker label on a product change's epic and on every one of its tasks (docs/decisions.md § D-02, item 3). change-propose puts it on the epic and the children inherit it; the general sweeps of the queue exclude it (`bd ready --exclude-label` in the bead skill and the fan-out-work agent), and change-plan, change-build, change-verify and change-finalize find the epic by it. Changing it here strands every open change: relabel their epics and tasks in the same change, and respell the label in every skill and agent that cites this key, which `npm run openspec:check` names. Decided 2026-09-23 with D-02; moved here 2026-09-23 by D-03.

assetLabels.asset:docs: a document that is neither the register nor the living spec: a README, a page under docs/, count-index.md
assetLabels.asset:environment: what a session runs on: the worktree script and its briefing template, the toolchain's versions, the harness's settings, the dev container
assetLabels.asset:gate: a gate, a hook, a test runner, or a job that runs one (lefthook.yml, .github/workflows/verify.yml)
assetLabels.asset:product: the product's code and its tests, under apps/
assetLabels.asset:prompt: CLAUDE.md, a skill, an agent, or a workflow script a skill runs
assetLabels.asset:spec: the living spec under openspec/specs/, or a change's proposal and delta specs
assetLabels.asset:tool: an emitter or a helper under tools/ or scripts/ that is not a gate

assetLabelsMeans: What an issue a run files `discovered-from` would fix: one label for each kind of file it would change, each key the label and each value what it covers (CLAUDE.md § The task store says when). Paired with its `foundAtLabels` label it is the recurrence signal the retired learning loop was to derive (docs/decisions.md § D-06): `bd count -l <a found-at label> --by-label` counts the pairs. An issue that fits none of these gets the label it needs added here first, with its date, in the change that files it. Renaming a label strands every issue that carries it: relabel them in the same change. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn); the eight values were fitted to the issues discovered from asdlc-openspec-zgh.

foundAtLabels.found:bead: while an issue was worked through the bead skill, or a lane of the fan-out-work agent
foundAtLabels.found:review: by looking back at a run after it ended: a prompt review, or a person or session reviewing a finished change

foundAtLabelsMeans: Where an issue a run files `discovered-from` was found: exactly one label, the stage that was running, each key the label and each value when it applies (CLAUDE.md § The task store says when). `found:review` is the count of what got through every stage and was caught only looking back. An issue filed before D-06 carries one only where its own text says which stage found it. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn), after a second opinion on the retirement pointed out that the loop's recurrence signal is the pair of where a correction was found and what it would fix.

rerouteLabels.reroute:build: change-verify sent work back to change-build: a gap in the code, or a finding the user made a new task
rerouteLabels.reroute:design: a later stage revised the design
rerouteLabels.reroute:plan: a later stage added a task to the epic
rerouteLabels.reroute:propose: a later stage revised the proposal or a delta spec

rerouteLabelsMeans: Labels on a product change's epic, one for each earlier stage a later stage sent the change back to, each key the label and each value when it applies (CLAUDE.md § Product work runs as OpenSpec-format changes says when). A label is a set: it records that the change went back, not how often. `bd count -t epic -l <specChangeLabel> --by-label` then answers how many changes needed their spec, design or plan reworked after the stage that wrote it, the rework a label on a found issue never sees because it lands as commits inside the change. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn), after the same second opinion showed that the calculator change's largest corrections, its spec revised during build and its design amended at verify, became no issue.
buildReviewLensesMeans: The reviewers `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs on one task of a product change, chosen by what the task mainly changes: each key an `assetLabels` key, each value the lens keys, one reviewer each. The parent session picks the key (`.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 3. Build it, and prove it). The lens prompts are the workflow's own, and a task adds only its focus to them, so no run reviews through more lenses than its set. `asset:spec` has no set: a task never edits its own delta specs, and a spec revision is the parent's, under that skill's § 5. A documentation, register or prompt task runs at most two lenses: the register-and-briefing task asdlc-openspec-zgh.6 ran three and spent 35 agents and 2,946,105 tokens to confirm 2 of the 9 findings it sent to skeptics, both minor (wf_f256bc20-ffb, a workflow state file outside this repository). A new key must be an `assetLabels` key, and a lens must exist in the workflow's library before a set names it; npm run workflows:selftest runs a clean control for every key and refuses a lens the workflow does not have. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics the workflow sends to confirm one finding of each severity. Each judges the finding against the delta specs, the design and the task, and answers upheld, refuted or unverified; a majority of those sent decides, and a finding with no majority goes back to the parent as unverified, never as refuted (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). A spec contradiction is always confirmed at `blocker`, because a confirmed one halts the run. The calculator change (asdlc-openspec-zgh) sent every finding to three: 58 findings went to 174 skeptics and 19 were upheld, and all 16 that its build runs confirmed were minor (the session's wf_*.json workflow state files, outside this repository; the figures are re-derived in a note on asdlc-openspec-d6b). Lowering `major` or `blocker` below 3 lets one vote decide a finding that blocks the task. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildReviewMaxRoundsMeans: The most review rounds one run of the workflow makes. A round reviews, confirms and fixes, and the next reviews that fix; after the last round's fix the run stops and reports the fix as unreviewed, and the parent reads its diff. In the calculator change no round after the second confirmed anything: its two third rounds sent 2 findings to skeptics and confirmed none (wf_ad92e5b6-d54 and wf_2d38608d-3a8, workflow state files outside this repository). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildReviewMajorSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a confirmed defect that earn another review round. A round that confirms none of these is the last: its confirmed minor defects are fixed and the run stops, so review does not loop on small findings, as `.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 5. What the build turns up keeps it from looping on coverage. No build run of the calculator change confirmed a finding above minor, yet five of them ran a second round and two a third (the session's wf_*.json workflow state files, outside this repository). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
promptReviewAnalysisMarkerMeans: The word that opens the first line of a run's analysis, a note on the issue or epic the run worked, followed by a space and the run id (`CLAUDE.md` § Prompt reviews says how both are written). `bd list --all --notes-contains` finds every analysis by it, so it must appear in no other note: changing it strands every analysis written under the old word, which no review then finds, so a change rewrites them or reviews them first. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewReadMarkerMeans: The word that opens the line a review appends to an issue for each analysis on it that the review read, followed by a space, the run id, a space, and the review's pull request or `no change`. An analysis is pending while no such line names its run id, so changing it makes every analysis already read pending again, and the next review reads them twice. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr); the maintainer chose an appended line over metadata on the issue, with the loss that a hand edit breaking a line miscounts.
promptReviewDueCountMeans: How many pending analyses make a review due, whatever their age; the closing step of every run checks it, and the reviewer checks it again when it starts (`CLAUDE.md` § Prompt reviews). It is a choice, not a measurement: eleven review pull requests were opened between 2026-09-24T23:47Z (#28) and 2026-09-25T23:10Z (#53), one per run that proposed a change (`gh pr list --state all --limit 100 --json number,title,createdAt`: the titles from #28 to #53 that cite no issue), so at that pace five analyses pend within about half a day, and each review reads at least that many runs side by side. Raising it makes each batch larger and each review later; 1 reviews every run, as D-05 did. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewDueAgeDaysMeans: How many days the oldest pending analysis may wait, read from the time in its run id, before a review is due however few are pending. It covers a slow week, when `promptReviewDueCount` analyses take longer to gather. Nothing checks it but the closing step of a run, so in a week when no prompt runs an analysis waits past it for the next run of any prompt; the maintainer chose that over a scheduler (D-08). It is a choice, not a measurement. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewHeldMarkerMeans: The word that opens a held line, which a review appends to the issue carrying a run's analysis for each finding that run showed and the review did not carry into its pull request: below the threshold, set aside by its file's agent, or on a branch the skeptics did not uphold (`CLAUDE.md` § Prompt reviews says how the line is written). The next review counts a finding from these lines, so changing the word strands every count kept under the old one, and each held finding starts again at one; a change rewrites them first. An analysis ends at the next line that opens with this word or either other marker. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm); the maintainer chose a line in the analysis notes, with the loss that a hand edit breaking one resets its count unnoticed.
promptReviewRecurrenceCountMeans: How many distinct runs must have shown a finding, those in the batch and those its held lines name, before a review proposes an edit for it, unless its severity is in `promptReviewMajorSeverities`. The reviewer's session applies it before the workflow runs and holds every finding below it, and `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` refuses one that reaches it. It is a choice, not a measurement: a research session on 2026-09-25 found no primary source for requiring a number of occurrences before an edit (asdlc-openspec-pnm). Where it loses: a one-off minor defect that costs an hour, and recurs a week later, is paid for twice before it is fixed. 1 proposes an edit for every finding, as D-08's review did. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm).
promptReviewMajorSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a finding a review proposes on one run, skipping `promptReviewRecurrenceCount`. The severities are those `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` § 2. Maintainability defines, so a prompt review and the pull-request reviewer grade on one scale. Adding `minor` removes the threshold; emptying the list makes every finding wait for a second run. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm).
promptReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` sends to judge one proposed edit, by its finding's severity, once the file's agent has committed it. Each reads the branch's diff and answers upheld, refuted or unverified to two questions: had the prompt said this, would the runs have gone differently; and does the edit break another path through the prompt, or another caller of it. A majority of those sent decides, and a branch merges only when every edit on it is upheld (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). The counts copy `buildReviewSkeptics`; where they lose, a batch of 5 major findings sends 15 skeptics. Lowering `major` or `blocker` below 3 lets one vote decide an edit every later run of the prompt reads. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm).
prReviewIssuePatternMeans: A tracker issue id, as a regular expression without anchors: this tracker's prefix, the hash, and a child's dotted suffix (`asdlc-openspec-zgh.9`). The reviewer reads the issues a pull request carries from the ids that match it inside the parentheses at the end of the pull request's title, and nowhere else: a body names follow-ups and related issues it does not carry. A title with none cites no issue, and a person merges that pull request (`docs/decisions.md` § D-07). Change it with the tracker's prefix. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewStatusContextMeans: The commit status the reviewer sets on a pull request's head commit: pending from the push until it has judged that commit, then success, failure or error with the reason in its description. It is what `gh pr checks --watch` waits on, so an agent watching its own pull request (`.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 6) reads the review's outcome as it reads any check. A verdict that needs a person sets success, not pending, so no watcher waits on a person. Renaming it strands the pending status on every open pull request until its next push. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewRequiredCheckMeans: The check run that must have passed on a commit before the reviewer acts on it: the one job of `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, whose check run carries the job's name. On a pull request's head it gates the review, so no review is spent on a head CI has refused; on `main`'s head it gates every merge, so after a bad merge the reviewer stops merging until `main` is green again. `npm run pr-review:check` refuses a `verify.yml` with no job of this name and a `pr-review.yml` whose `workflow_run` does not name that workflow. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewLabelsMeans: The labels the reviewer reads and writes on a pull request, each key its role and each value its spelling. `changes`: a dimension failed, and the author fixes the branch; the next push is reviewed again. `human`: nothing failed, and a person decides, because the risk is high, a criterion could not be verified, or the title cites no issue. `approved`: a person approves the merge of the head commit the reviewer last judged. It counts only when a person with a permission in `prReviewApproverPermissions` applied it after that verdict, and an agent never applies it (`CLAUDE.md` § Git workflow). The reviewer creates the three if they are missing. Renaming one means renaming it on the repository in the same change, and `npm run pr-review:check` refuses a `pr-review.yml` that filters on another spelling of `approved`. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewApproverPermissionsMeans: The repository permissions, as GitHub's collaborator-permission endpoint names them, of an account whose application of the approval label counts. A bot's never does. GitHub cannot tell a person from an agent acting with that person's credentials, which is `docs/decisions.md` § R-01. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewBlockingSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a maintainability finding that fail the dimension. A `minor` finding is posted in the review and blocks nothing, so the reviewer does not hold a merge on wording. The severities themselves are defined in `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` § 2. Maintainability. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewContextPathsMeans: The files held to the context-engineering rubric: what an agent reads to decide what to do, meaning the rules, the prompts, the documents, the specs and the constants they cite. Every other file is held to the product rubric. `*` matches within one directory, `**` across directories, and `**/` also matches none. A file is classed by its path at the pull request's head, and the brief names each file's class, so the reviewer does not choose. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).

prReviewHighRiskPaths..github/**: the workflows: what runs with the repository's token and secrets, this reviewer among them
prReviewHighRiskPaths..claude/settings.json: the hooks every session runs, the guards among them
prReviewHighRiskPaths.AGENTS.md: the pointer another harness follows to those rules
prReviewHighRiskPaths.docs/decisions.md: a recorded decision, which is the maintainer's to make
prReviewHighRiskPaths.package-lock.json: the dependency tree every gate and the product run on

prReviewHighRiskPathsMeans: The floor under the reviewer's risk judgement: a pull request that adds, changes, deletes or renames a file matching one of these globs is high risk whatever the reviewer says, and merges only on a person's approval. Each key is a glob, matched as `prReviewContextPaths` says, and each value is the reason the review comment gives. The reviewer can raise a pull request to high but never lower one below this floor, so no pull request can argue its way past a person into changing CI, this reviewer or the rules. Removing a line lets pull requests that change that file merge without a person, and this key is itself high risk (`prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewHighRiskJsonKeysMeans: The second half of the floor: top-level keys of committed JSON files whose value a pull request changes (added, removed or different, compared as parsed JSON) make it high risk. A trailing `*` matches any key with that prefix. It exists because the whole file is too wide: most pull requests that add a gate add a script to `package.json`, and many change another key of this file, and neither needs a person. A dependency, an install-script permission, the engine floor, or a key the reviewer decides by does. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewMergeMethodMeans: How the reviewer merges: the method GitHub's merge endpoint takes. It is `rebase` because `docs/decisions.md` § D-02, item 6, rebase-merges a change's pull request so `npm run worktree:gc` can prove its branch reached the trunk, and the repository allows no other method. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
